newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong public favour judge over tycoon.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong public favour judge over tycoon.

text.p: Hong Kong people favour a retired judge to be their first post-colonial leader, not the shipping magnate who swept the first round ballot for the job, an opinion poll showed on Saturday.
The telephone poll of 698 people, conducted by the Chinese University of Hong Kong after Friday's first round vote, put former chief justice Yang Ti Liang ahead of tycoon Tung Chee-hwa in popularity.
If an election were held by universal suffrage, Yang would get 35.7 percent and Tung 33.5 percent, the poll showed.
However, the appointment will be made by a 400-member Selection Committee formed under China's supervision.
Tung received 206 votes from the committee in the initial round of balloting on Friday for election of the territory's first chief executive, versus 82 for Yang.
His victory made it seem inevitable Tung would govern the territory after China takes it back from Britain at midnight next June 30. The final vote will be on December 11.
